video_title: Can the Knicks Break the 8-Year No-Repeat Streak? | Rachel Nichols & Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' roster continuity and championship potential
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks enter the season with largely the same roster that they had last season.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: The Knicks enter the season with largely the same roster that they had last season. They lost Mitchell Robinson, they replaced him with Andre Drummond, but the core of their team is back, the core of their team is in its prime.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: Not only is this an eight-year run, that is the longest run of non-repeat champions, individual champions, since the 70s in the NBA. So this isn't just parity, it is a historical level of parity.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' starting five and bench depth as championship assets
quotes.excerpt: I think they have a fabulous chance to repeat because they've got their starting five.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I think they have a fabulous chance to repeat because they've got their starting five. And that starting five unit is definitely more than the sum of its parts. This is a team, this starting five is a team, and the key bench guys that are part of that real heart unit, they signed those guys too. Alvarado they signed, Landry Shamet they signed, Mike Brown is in his second year, everybody knows his system.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: It was a very uneven regular season last year. There were some real glow streaks and part of it was attributed to the fact that not everybody had a real role. We heard that from Carl-Anthony Towns and Mike Brown was putting in a new system. That's not the case anymore.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' path through the Eastern Conference playoffs
quotes.excerpt: They are able to roll through a relatively easy Eastern Conference playoff field.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Among the reasons the Knicks are defending champs is that they are able to roll through a relatively easy Eastern Conference playoff field. It's tougher now with the 76ers, they are a bit of an unknown, some other teams at the bottom are certainly going to improve. Wins generally will be a little harder to come by, but it's still the junior varsity conference compared to the West.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: Towns played 75 games last year. He was a rock. They don't win the title without Carl-Anthony Towns. He was phenomenal in the playoffs.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating the Knicks' roster changes and Mitchell Robinson's role
quotes.excerpt: Mitchell Robinson was kind of an institution there in New York.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Mitchell Robinson was kind of an institution there in New York. You knew you could get 20 good minutes out of Mitchell Robinson. You knew what you were going to get. I don't know if you know that necessarily with Andre Drummond. They went out and they signed James Wiseman. Mike Brown apparently likes James Wiseman, maybe they can be the team that coaxes whatever it is out of the former number two overall pick.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I think they have a fabulous chance to repeat because they've got their starting five. And that starting five unit is definitely more than the sum of its parts.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The financial implications of a potential Carl-Anthony Towns extension
quotes.excerpt: That's a lot of money to potentially be committing to Carl-Anthony Towns.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: The contract with Towns is interesting because that's a lot of money to potentially be committing to Carl-Anthony Towns. If you're the Knicks, do you want to commit four years, 275-ish, I guess what it would be to him? I guess your question is, would it be a distraction?

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: He can be a free agent at the end of this season. And if he has a good season, he's not leaving 61 million on the table if he gets that much or more from someone else.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's stance on his contract and free agency
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brunson's already come out and said, I am not taking a discount this time.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: Jalen Brunson's already come out and said, I am not taking a discount this time. He's like, I've earned my money, which he absolutely has. However, you just have to calculate for it.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: In a vacuum, I'd say sign the guy. Give him his money, bring him back. You've got something good going on here.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The evolution of NBA player contracts and salary caps
quotes.excerpt: I was doing a pod with Evan and we were talking about like LeBron's max back in the Miami days.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I was doing a pod with Evan and we were talking about like LeBron's max back in the Miami days. And he was like, how much did LeBron make? And I think I said something like 40, 50 million. It was like 17. That was just like 15 years ago.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: Well, remember, the TV contract going into the 2016 season exploded. So huge, huge jumps. And now that these guys are making way more money in their careers than they could ever hope that their grandchildren's grandchildren will use.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The trend of players taking less money to build championship teams
quotes.excerpt: If you want a guy to take less money, explain where that money's going.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: If you want a guy to take less money, explain where that money's going. That guy is not going to take less money so your billionaire owner can pocket a few extra bucks and avoid paying the luxury tax. If you tell Carl-Anthony Towns, we're going to take this money, we're going to devote more of it to Brunson because he's owed it and responsible for it, we're going to bring Josh Hart back, we're not going to have to trade OG Anunoby, here's what happens when you take a couple of bucks less.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I wouldn't even phrase it, I mean I think everything you say is true. And you're right, guys taking a pay cut want to know where the money is going.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Knicks' vulnerability compared to other championship contenders
quotes.excerpt: I do think they're more vulnerable than some other champions were coming into the year.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I do think they're more vulnerable than some other champions were coming into the year. If I just look back at like Oklahoma City, I definitely thought they were the favorite to repeat. Boston, based on what they did, I definitely thought they were a favorite to repeat. Even go back to Denver, like they had found something. I don't feel the exact same way about New York.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: When you said the West is undoubtedly the better conference and the East is junior varsity, I don't know if I agree with that.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The competitive landscape of the Western Conference
quotes.excerpt: I think the top two teams in the West are elite above everyone else.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I think the top two teams in the West are elite above everyone else in terms of what's on paper and what they've shown us so far. Look, you've got Giannis and Bam in Miami. And I know that might be it. Well, yeah, I mean you got Curry to take care of some of the shooting.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Let's do this thought experiment then. How far down in the Western Conference standings do you have to find a team that you wouldn't make the favorite to win the Eastern Conference?

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The shift in conference strength and the 'squishy middle'
quotes.excerpt: I used to say the East has a squishy middle. Like, now the West has a squishy middle.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I used to say the East has a squishy middle. Like, now the West has a squishy middle. And the East is teams that are going to be tough to get wins. Look, you've got Giannis and Bam in Miami. And I know that might be it. Well, yeah, I mean you got Curry to take care of some of the shooting.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I'd make Denver with Jokic, I don't think anybody in the East is beating Jokic in a seven-game series.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating the 76ers' roster and championship potential
quotes.excerpt: Philadelphia, I have questions about how all those pieces are going to fit together.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Philadelphia, I have questions about how all those pieces are going to fit together. But I can tell you that on paper, it seems like a better roster than last year.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: You are arguing with the best player of all time and an All-NBA, should have been first-team guy.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Charlotte Hornets' offseason and future outlook
quotes.excerpt: Charlotte kind of mailed in the offseason. Like they sent LaMelo Ball out, they sent Miles.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Charlotte kind of mailed in the offseason. Like they sent LaMelo Ball out, they sent Miles. I think they just, they're kind of resetting on the fly to me. Like maybe if Kanipple takes another step forward, Brandon Miller becomes an All-NBA type of guy, maybe. But they might actually be one of those that takes a step back.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: Cleveland thinks it's better.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Cleveland Cavaliers' roster and potential for growth
quotes.excerpt: Cleveland does think it's better. Peyton Watson, they feel the better. Maybe, but I like Denver with Jokic.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Cleveland does think it's better. Peyton Watson, they feel the better. Maybe, but I like Denver with Jokic. I don't think anybody in the East is beating Jokic in a seven-game series. Houston, we'll see, but I think they've got a lot of room for organic growth with Thompson and Reed Sheppard getting better, Fred VanVleet back again.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I'm not going to say that's a championship roster right now, but I definitely believe it's a better roster than last year.
